title: QUMem: Personalized Memory for Query-Conditioned User-State Inference in LLM Agents

visual_explainer.blocker: A QUMem-specific GPT Image attempt ignored the grounded single-paper brief and rendered unrelated Agent Memory Radar dashboard/status UI with fabricated repository and paper metadata. The same current-run identity failure had already occurred twice for HyperSkill, so further QUMem retries were stopped to avoid publishing ungrounded art. GitHub binary publication is available; blocker is image-generator paper identity/grounding.

analysis.tldr: QUMem separates archival representation from query-time personalization: it builds semantically coherent episodes, decomposes each into independently retrievable facts, preferences/constraints, and transferable insights, then uses explicit information-need, retrieval-planning, and user-state-inference stages to construct the current task-relevant user state rather than returning top-k memories directly.
analysis.problem: Long-term personalization fails when fixed memory boundaries split events, when multiple user signals from one episode are stored as one indivisible item, and when the current query is used as a single similarity key even though valid preferences may be distributed across time, context-dependent, or superseded by later evidence.
analysis.core_idea: First segment dialogue history into variable-length episodes using semantic continuity, then decompose each episode into factual, preference/constraint, and transferable-insight memories with source links and temporal positions. At query time, an information-need agent specifies what historical state must be verified, a retrieval-planning agent rewrites those needs into multiple typed-store queries, and a user-state agent jointly interprets the retrieved evidence into chronological facts, currently applicable preference evolution, and transferable principles for the downstream response/action model.

memory_design.write: Use a lightweight semantic-continuity classifier to maintain an open episode and finalize it at event boundaries. For each finalized episode, run three type-conditioned LLM extractions to create independently retrievable factual, preference/constraint, and transferable-insight memories while retaining the source episode, supporting turns, and latest temporal position.
memory_design.organize: Keep complete source episodes for event context plus typed atomic memory stores for reusable evidence. Each atomic item has content, type, temporal position, and explicit evidence links so query-time reasoning can trace validity back to the interaction history.
memory_design.read: Separate three query-time decisions: identify information needs; plan multiple rewritten queries over selected memory types; merge/deduplicate candidates and jointly infer a query-conditioned user state containing chronological facts, preference evolution/current applicability, and transferable principles.
memory_design.update_forget: New interaction history extends episodes and creates new typed memories. The paper models temporal validity during query-time state inference but does not center on explicit deletion, revocation, or long-horizon conflict-repair operations over stored memories.

compared_to: component ablations removing episode construction, typed decomposition, or query-time user-state reconstruction
analysis.evidence: On PersonaMem, QUMem improves GPT-4o-mini overall accuracy from the strongest baseline's 52.99% to 61.02% and Gemini-3.5-flash from 63.29% to 70.58%. On KnowU-Bench it reaches 17.4% overall success versus 12.8% for the strongest baseline, with higher score and interaction efficiency as well. The cleanest mechanism evidence is the PersonaMem ablation: 61.02 full, 58.38 without episode construction, 57.11 without typed memory decomposition, and 54.51 without query-time user-state reconstruction, making reconstruction/planned evidence interpretation the largest contributor. Construction accounting reports 27.1 builds and 81.4 generative LLM calls per 100 dialogue turns, plus 1,221.2 construction tokens per turn; this excludes the local continuity-classifier cost.
analysis.why_it_matters: QUMem strengthens a key radar distinction: the stored memory object and the consumer-facing state should not be conflated. Its largest ablation effect comes after retrieval, where distributed evidence is interpreted into a current user state. That makes personalization a state-reconstruction problem rather than simply a better top-k problem, and provides a concrete bridge from persistent memory to acting personalized agents through KnowU-Bench.
limitations: The full package changes segmentation, persistent representation, retrieval planning, and query-time interpretation; the component ablations identify contribution but do not fully match all alternative interfaces stage by stage.
The dynamic episode boundary classifier is trained on LoCoMo data and its transfer to very different dialogue/task distributions is not independently stress-tested.
KnowU-Bench end-to-end success remains low in absolute terms, especially on hard tasks, so memory-state improvements do not solve personalized execution reliability.
Construction-cost reporting excludes the local semantic-continuity classifier and does not provide a complete end-to-end serving-cost comparison including the three query-time agents.
